sources.entry: NetAlertX - Network intruder and presence detector. Scans for devices connected to your network and alerts you if new and unknown devices are found. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: NetAlertX is a self-hosted network visibility and asset intelligence platform that discovers connected devices, flags unknown or unauthorized hardware, and sends alerts.
summary.what_it_does: It continuously scans local networks to build an inventory of connected devices and tracks connection state changes and IP address management (IPAM) drift. The README names discovery methods including arp-scan, Pi-hole database and DHCP lease imports, generic DHCP lease import, UniFi controller import, and SNMP-enabled router import, with more available as plugins. Notifications can go to more than 80 services via Apprise, or through native Pushsafer, Pushover, or NTFY publishers. A workflows module can auto-assign new devices, group devices by vendor, unarchive devices that come back online, or delete devices. Sync Nodes let distributed collectors send inventory to a central hub for multi-site or MSP monitoring, and the README also mentions Prometheus metrics export, webhooks, a GraphQL/API layer, and Home Assistant integration.
use_cases: detect unknown devices on my home network
monitor multiple client sites from one dashboard
track shadow IT and unauthorized hardware
get alerts when new devices join the network
track IP address changes and IPAM drift
feed device presence data into Home Assistant
notable: Sync Nodes for distributed collection from VLANs, branch offices, and remote sites into a central hub
Workflows module for automated device categorization and cleanup policies
Plugin system for building custom scanners
Data stays local by default; no external data transmission unless notifications or integrations are configured
Prometheus metrics export and NOC-style wallboard dashboards
caveats: Some scanners such as ARP may not detect devices on different subnets, per the troubleshooting section
Wi-Fi-only networks may need alternate scanners for accurate detection
Requires elevated network capabilities (NET_RAW, NET_ADMIN) and host networking in the documented Docker setup
Supported browsers are listed as Chrome and Firefox only
